top_categories.workout_context: 348 miles. Your legs will beg to quit after 120. This trains the power output you need from mile 130 onward.
Race-pace efforts that mimic Race Around Austria's demands. Pacing, fueling, and tactical decisions under fatigue. Practice the race before August.
At Race Around Austria, changes in grade or pace can lift effort above threshold before it settles again. Over-unders train that transition while you keep riding.
21,325ft of climbing on grades that change every minute. You need to switch from seated to standing without losing rhythm.
61ft/mi signals a climbing-heavy course. Sustained sub-threshold and threshold work builds the steady power needed without turning the opening climb into the day’s hardest effort.
21,325ft of climbing makes aerobic ceiling relevant when the grade or pace changes. VO2max work supports those hard moments; sustained climbing and conservative pacing remain the spine.

Race Around Austria's mixed terrain rewards road-specific control. Practice smooth gear and cadence changes, accelerate deliberately out of corners, and settle quickly back into sustainable power for 348 miles.
Every hard session works better with a bigger aerobic base. At 348 miles, base fitness is the difference between racing and surviving.
348 miles rewards fat oxidation. This volume work shifts your fuel mix so you're still burning fat at hour 5, not bonking at hour 3.
Endurance with intensity spikes baked in. Exactly what 21,325ft of climbing on mixed terrain does to your power file on race day.
88–92% FTP is where you'll spend the hardest sustained miles of Race Around Austria. Train it until it feels boring.
Low-cadence force work supports 21,325ft of climbing when the grade lowers cadence. Practice controlled torque while preserving good form.

race_overlay.nutrition: Ultra-distance fueling for 348 miles requires a practiced resupply plan built around confirmed course services and available commercial stops. Rehearse frequent carbohydrate intake on long rides, then scale the plan to intensity, sleep strategy, tolerance, and real food across the full event. Carry redundant fuel and avoid applying a short-event hourly target or fixed total-calorie estimate to a multi-day race.
race_overlay.altitude: Altitude may change sustainable power and recovery at Race Around Austria. Use conservative pacing and test any travel strategy before the event.
race_overlay.terrain: The course profile at Race Around Austria rewards specific practice. Include regular rides on mixed terrain to build confidence.

pack_summary: This 10-workout pack focuses on Durability, Race Simulation, and Over Under to prepare you for 348 miles of mixed terrain in St. Georgen im Attergau, Austria (CHALLENGE category route — the flagship Extreme race covers ~2,200km/30,000m around all of Austria).
